title: You keep saying you don’t have time.
paragraphs: You keep saying you don’t have time.
But that’s not true.

You had time to scroll.
Time to delay.
Time to sit in the silence and feel that quiet conviction rising in your chest… and then ignore it.
God saw it.
You knew.
And somewhere deep down, you’re aware this isn’t a time problem.
It’s a priority problem.
Because when something actually matters to you, you find a way. You rearrange your day. You sacrifice sleep. You cancel plans. You move mountains for what you value.
But when it comes to God?
You negotiate.

“Later.”
“Tomorrow.”
“When things slow down.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
There is no “later” promised to you.
Scripture doesn’t say, “Seek the Lord when your schedule clears.”
It says:
“Seek the Lord while He may be found; call upon Him while He is near.” — Isaiah 55:6
Read that again.
While He may be found.
That means there is a window.
And you’ve been treating it like it’s permanent.

You wake up rushed.
You move through your day distracted.
You fill every gap with noise.
And when the day ends, you’re too tired to pray, too numb to listen, too distant to feel anything at all.
But you still say you love God.
You still say you believe.
So let’s be honest for a moment—
If someone watched your life on silent, without hearing your words…
Would they see that God is your priority?
Or just your idea?
Because Jesus didn’t say, “Fit Me in when you can.”
He said:
“Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.” — Matthew 6:33
First.

Not after your goals.
Not after your comfort.
Not after your distractions.
First.
That’s where everything shifts.
Because when God is not first, everything else becomes disordered.

Your peace becomes fragile.
Your identity becomes unstable.
Your decisions become self-centered.
And your soul starts drying out—quietly, slowly, dangerously.
You feel it, don’t you?

That restlessness.
That lack of clarity.
That spiritual dullness you can’t quite explain.
It’s not because God is distant.
It’s because He’s not first.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
And here’s the weight of it…
You don’t drift away from God because you decided to abandon Him.
You drift because you kept choosing other things first.
Over and over again.
Until one day, He’s no longer central—just occasional.
But God doesn’t accept leftovers.
He doesn’t compete for attention.
He calls for surrender.
“For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” — Matthew 6:21
So where is your treasure right now?
Be honest.

Is it comfort?
Validation?
Money?
Control?
Or is it Christ?
Because your calendar already reveals your answer.
And this is where everything breaks open—
You don’t need more hours in your day.
You need a reordered heart.
You need repentance.

Not just feeling bad.
Not just saying sorry.
But turning.

Turning from a life where God is secondary…
to a life where He is everything.
Because the Gospel isn’t about managing your time better.
It’s about dying to yourself and being made new.
“Whoever wants to be My disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow Me.” — Luke 9:23
Daily.
Not when it’s convenient.
Not when it feels easy.
Daily.

That means choosing Him when your flesh wants comfort.
Choosing Him when your mind wants distraction.
Choosing Him when no one else is watching.
That’s where transformation happens.
And here’s the hope you’ve been missing—
God is not waiting to punish you for wasted time.
He’s waiting to restore you.

To take what’s been disordered…
and realign it through grace.
“Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord. — Malachi 3:7
But you have to return.

Not halfway.
Not later.
Now.
Because every moment you delay is a moment you’re choosing something else over Him.
And you feel that tension right now.
That pull.
That quiet voice saying, “This is about you.”
Don’t ignore it this time.
Say it plainly:
“I’ve been putting God second.”
Type it.
Own it.
Let it break your pride.
Then do something different—
Reorder your life starting today.

Open the Word before your phone.
Pray before you plan.
Listen before you speak.
And watch what happens when God is no longer squeezed into your life…
but becomes the center of it.
Stay close.
There’s more truth like this waiting—deeper correction, clearer direction, real spiritual growth that doesn’t leave you the same.
Walk this path with me.
